name: Domain Real Estate Partners
summary: Domain's public footprint is larger than its low press profile suggests. Its own website (statistics as of Oct 31, 2026) gives the scale: $6.7B+ current gross asset value, about $18.2B committed since 2015 across 825 projects, 33 active builder and developer partners, 29 states and 91 MSAs, and a full team page with 21 named people including 2025-2026 hires from Lennar's land finance group and a TPG Angelo Gordon platform. Named builder links are thin and Lennar-heavy: Lennar's chairman named Domain on the March 2026 earnings call and South Florida deed coverage shows DW Partners land-banking for Lennar ($164.5M Sunrise site, Jan 2026); the only other builder names come from a May 2024 one-pager (Pulte, Toll, Clayton, Ashton Woods, David Weekley) and a 2015 Hovnanian release. The most exposed material is on the capital side: a publicly downloadable 2024 one-pager states a 13% median rate, 41-month median term, net returns of roughly 11% to 16% a year and the fee and leverage assumptions; the CIO has said on podcasts that the fund annualizes at 14% to 15%, that pricing is low double digits, and that insurance private placements (including a $200M five- and seven-year note deal in Q3 2025) are investment-grade rated; PGIM has announced more than $4B across seven deals; and SEC filings show fund-by-fund raises (Solaris $565M from 41 investors, Metric $333M, Evergreen $205M) against DW regulatory AUM of $2.27B. Builder SEC filings reveal essentially nothing about Domain's option fees or deposits: full-text search finds the firm's name in only one builder filing, from 2015. Not everything requested could be checked: the shared web-search budget ran out part-way, so per-builder trade-press and deed searches, rating-agency sites and land-banker rankings are listed in gaps rather than covered.

facts.fact: Domain's homepage describes the firm as a capital partner to the U.S. homebuilding industry since 2015, providing capital for residential land acquisition, development and construction. Headline statistics shown: founded 2015; 825 projects financed since inception; $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value; 33 active homebuilder and land developer partners.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage (statistics footnoted as of October 31, 2026)

facts.fact: Domain's homepage 'Our Platform' block states 29 active states, 91 active MSAs, $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value and about $18.2B gross capital committed since inception, footnoted as portfolio statistics as of October 31, 2026.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage, Our Platform

facts.fact: Domain publishes three strategies. Land Banking: it acquires fully entitled land and funds 100% of horizontal development into finished lots; it says it primarily partners with Top 60 U.S. homebuilders, 'predominantly the Top 25'. A&D Lending: senior-secured, non-recourse first-mortgage loans to land developers delivering finished lots to national and regional builders, typically under pre-sale commitments. Vertical Financing: financing to Top 200 U.S. homebuilders for vertical home construction.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage, Our Investment Strategies

facts.fact: Domain's Builders page says it partners with well-capitalized public and private homebuilders and land developers nationwide and seeks long-term relationships with proven operators. No builder is named on the page, and no pricing or terms are published anywhere on the site.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Builders page

facts.fact: Domain's Investors page offers only a login link to a Juniper Square investor portal (data room, fund documents, reporting) and an investor-relations email address; no fund names, sizes or investor names are published. The site footer says any offer is made only to qualified investors by private placement memorandum.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Investors page

facts.fact: Domain's published office address is 520 Madison Ave, 21st Floor, New York, NY 10022, and the site copyright line reads Domain Real Estate Partners, LLC (2026).
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, footer

facts.fact: DW Partners' own Firm page lists 'Domain Homebuilder Finance' as one of four strategies (with RMBS, CMBS and CRE Lending), active since 2015, with two products: land banking (off-balance-sheet financing tied to builder sales pace) and first-mortgage loans for land acquisition and infrastructure development. DW's homepage describes DW as an employee-owned alternative asset manager founded in 2009 that invests in bonds and loans collateralized by real estate.
facts.source_title: DW Partners website, Firm page (copyright 2026)

facts.fact: DW Partners' Form ADV (other-than-annual amendment dated 2026-05-01) lists 'Domain Real Estate Partners, LLC' as an other business name of DW Partners, LP, and its Schedule D note states that Domain Real Estate Partners, LLC is an entity within DW's operational structure that executes DW's residential homebuilder finance strategy, and that the individuals who use the Domain name are DW employees under DW's supervisory and compliance program. In legal terms the public record shows Domain as a DW strategy / business name rather than a separately registered adviser.
facts.source_title: DW Partners, LP Form ADV Part 1A (CRD 155459), Schedule D Section 1.B and Miscellaneous, filed 2026-05-01

facts.fact: DW Partners, LP reported regulatory assets under management of $2,273,017,018 across 21 accounts, all discretionary, in its Form ADV dated 2026-05-01. By client type, $2,272,951,218 is in 20 pooled investment vehicles; no assets are reported under the 'insurance companies' client category.
facts.source_title: DW Partners, LP Form ADV Part 1A, Items 5.D and 5.F, filed 2026-05-01

facts.fact: DW's Form ADV (2026-05-01) lists four Domain-named private funds, all typed as real estate funds: Domain Solaris Fund, LP (gross asset value $654.7M, about 37 beneficial owners, $1M minimum); Domain Metric Fund, LP ($331.9M, about 4 owners, $1M minimum); Domain Evergreen Fund, LP ($172.1M, about 7 owners, $5M minimum); Domain Evergreen Onshore Fund, LP ($27.9M, 1 owner, $5M minimum). Sum of the four gross asset values = $1,186.6M (calculated: 654.7 + 331.9 + 172.1 + 27.9). Auditor shown for each is Ernst & Young; custodian State Street Bank and Trust.
facts.source_title: DW Partners, LP Form ADV Part 1A, Schedule D Section 7.B.(1), filed 2026-05-01

facts.fact: Public gap between two published scale figures: the Domain website shows $6.7B+ 'current investment gross asset value' (Oct 31, 2026) while DW's Form ADV shows $2.27B of regulatory AUM (May 2026) and about $1.19B of gross assets in Domain-named funds. Domain's own May 2024 one-pager footnote explains its 'strategy assets' as a combination of assets advised by DW and assets serviced by Domain Servicing, LLC, and PGIM has separately announced funding of more than $4B of land banking through Domain. A reader can therefore see that most of the deployed capital sits outside DW-advised funds (difference 6.7 - 2.27 = about $4.4B; inference from the cited figures, not a company statement).
facts.source_title: Domain website homepage statistics, compared with DW Form ADV 2026-05-01 and Domain one-pager May 2024

facts.fact: Domain Solaris Fund, LP (Delaware LP organized 2023, c/o DW Partners) Form D/A signed 2026-08-12: first sale 2023-08-01, indefinite offering, $564,780,000 sold to 41 investors, $1,000,000 minimum, Rule 506(b) and Section 3(c)(7), no sales compensation. General partner: DW General Partner, LLC. Signed by Houdin Honarvar as authorized signatory of the GP.
facts.source_title: Domain Solaris Fund, LP Form D/A filed 2026-08-12

facts.fact: Domain Metric Fund, LP Form D/A signed 2025-12-23: first sale 2018-12-14, indefinite offering, $333,400,000 sold to 3 investors, $1,000,000 minimum, Rule 506(b) and Section 3(c)(7). Placement agent listed: Blue Sand Securities LLC (Scottsdale, AZ); $78,126 of sales commissions, noted as paid by DW Partners, LP rather than from proceeds. Related persons: DW General Partner, LLC; DW Partners, LP (investment manager); David Warren.
facts.source_title: Domain Metric Fund, LP Form D/A filed 2025-12-23

facts.fact: Domain Evergreen Fund, LP (Delaware LP organized 2025) Form D/A signed 2026-03-13: first sale 2025-03-03, indefinite offering, $205,086,306 sold to 9 investors, $5,000,000 minimum, Rule 506(b), no sales compensation. Its sister Domain Evergreen Onshore Fund, LP (same dates) reported $23,400,000 sold to 1 investor.
facts.source_title: Domain Evergreen Fund, LP Form D/A filed 2026-03-13 (Onshore fund: CIK 2060665, accession 0002060665-26-000003)

facts.fact: Domain Real Estate Offshore Fund I, LP Form D/A signed 2022-12-22 (latest on file; older than 24 months, no newer filing found): first sale 2019-12-27, $500,000,000 total offering, $356,113,625 sold to 8 investors, $5,000,000 minimum, Section 3(c)(7). General partner DW Domain GP, LLC; investment manager DW Partners, LP. The fund does not appear among the private funds in DW's 2026 Form ADV.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Offshore Fund I, LP Form D/A filed 2022-12-22

facts.fact: Domain Real Estate Fund II, LP (Delaware LP organized 2023) filed a single Form D on 2023-05-04: $5,000,000 offered and sold to 1 investor, first sale 2023-05-01, offering not intended to last more than a year. Older than 24 months with no later amendment.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Fund II, LP Form D filed 2023-05-04

facts.fact: Domain's own Press page summarises the PGIM press release of May 26, 2026: PGIM and Domain have surpassed $4 billion of U.S. residential land-banking transactions across seven deals since their partnership began, using asset-based, non-bank capital, with Domain sourcing, underwriting, closing and managing each deal.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Press page (PGIM release, May 26, 2026)

facts.fact: Bisnow (May 26, 2026) reported that PGIM, Prudential Financial's asset manager, completed more than $4 billion of land-banking deals through its partnership with Domain Real Estate Partners LLC, that the partnership began in 2025 ('last year'), and that seven residential land bank transactions had been financed. Quoted: Oliver Nisenson (PGIM head of private asset-based finance), Gabriel Rivera (PGIM co-head of securitized products) and Bob Clark (Domain Chief Investment Officer). No builders, deal sizes or pricing were disclosed.
facts.source_title: Bisnow, 'PGIM Finances $4B In U.S. Land-Banking Deals With Partner Domain Real Estate', May 26, 2026

facts.fact: Alternative Credit Investor (May 26, 2026) reported the PGIM-Domain partnership targets national housebuilders, sits inside PGIM's private asset-based finance platform, and that Domain had more than $6bn deployed across its portfolio at that time. Simple average per transaction = about $571M ($4,000M / 7; calculated).
facts.source_title: Alternative Credit Investor, 'PGIM and Domain hit $4bn in US land-banking deals', May 26, 2026

facts.fact: A Domain one-pager (data as of April 30, 2024; prepared by DW Partners) is openly downloadable from InsuranceAUM.com and shows the then-active portfolio: $1.77bn strategy assets, $5bn total budgeted project costs, about 60,000 total lots across 52 MSAs, 159 land banks, 6 mortgage loans, 1 joint venture, 23 homebuilders and land developers, a 13% median interest rate and a 41-month median term. The document's own disclaimer says it is not intended for general distribution, yet it is reachable without login. Tagged Inferred only because the data is more than 24 months old (primary document, opened); it is the only public document found that states a rate and a term.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024 (hosted on InsuranceAUM.com)

facts.fact: The same May 2024 one-pager publishes monthly net performance for 2016 through March 2024, with calendar-year net returns between 10.60% (2017) and 15.70% (2018) and 13.63% for 2023. Its footnote discloses the model fee load used (0.50% management fee, 0.50% servicing fee, 10% performance fee over an 8% hurdle with 50/50 catch-up) and that third-party leverage has been applied since December 2017 at rates ranging from 4.75% to SOFR + 4.00%. Tagged Inferred only because the document is more than 24 months old.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024, Historical Net Performance and footnotes

facts.fact: The May 2024 one-pager gives the strategy inception as August 2015, describes land banks as off-balance-sheet financing delivering finished lots on a 'just in time' basis matched to estimated sales pace, and says deals are directly sourced from builders and developers and underwritten and managed by an in-house team. It names clients: public builders Lennar, Pulte and Toll Brothers; private builders Clayton Homes, Ashton Woods and David Weekley; land developers Eisenhower Property Group and Glenmont Development. Tagged Inferred only because the document is more than 24 months old.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024, Investment Strategy and Partnerships

facts.fact: Growth visible from Domain's own published figures: strategy assets $1.77bn (Apr 30, 2024, one-pager) to $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value (Oct 31, 2026, website), roughly 3.8x in 30 months (6.7 / 1.77; calculated; the two metrics are labelled differently so the comparison is approximate). Counterparties grew from 23 to 33 and MSAs from 52 to 91 over the same period.
facts.source_title: Domain website homepage (Oct 31, 2026) compared with Domain one-pager (Apr 30, 2024)

facts.fact: InsuranceAUM.com lists Domain Real Estate Partners as a Platinum Partner with a public profile: founded 2015, 825 projects financed with over $18bn of project costs, products described as structured lot purchase options (land banking), non-recourse loans and project-level equity investments, and '$3BN' assets under management footnoted as of 10/31/2026. The page names John Mackin (Partner) as contact and links two podcasts with Bob Clark (Oct 28, 2024 and Nov 6, 2025). The channel choice shows insurers are a target investor audience.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com, Domain Real Estate Partners profile page

facts.fact: George Smith Partners' Landscape podcast page for 'The Land Banker's View of the Housing Market' (dated October 27, 2026 on Domain's Press page) describes Domain as one of the largest land bankers and land lenders in the country, with roughly $6.7 billion 'in the ground' and more than $17 billion funded across 750+ projects, all in for-sale residential. Guest: Bob Clark, listed as Founding Partner, DW Partners and CIO, Domain Real Estate Partners.
facts.source_title: George Smith Partners, The Landscape Podcast, 'The Land Banker's View of the Housing Market'

facts.fact: The GSP podcast show notes (Oct 2026) say the episode covers how Domain prices deals on the builder relationship rather than deal by deal, that banks are generally not Domain's competition, that insurance capital is moving into senior land debt, and that new land bankers entering in 2026 have compressed spreads. No numeric pricing is given in the notes.
facts.source_title: George Smith Partners, The Landscape Podcast show notes

facts.fact: Domain's Press page lists five items only: the GSP podcast (Oct 27, 2026), the PGIM release (May 26, 2026), Lennar's Q1 FY2026 earnings call mention (Mar 13, 2026), and two InsuranceAUM podcasts with Bob Clark (Nov 6, 2025 and Oct 28, 2024). DW Partners' own Press page lists nothing about Domain, homebuilders or land banking (latest item Feb 2022).
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Press page; DW Partners Press page checked the same day

facts.fact: On Lennar's Q1 fiscal 2026 earnings call (March 13, 2026) Executive Chairman Stuart Miller named Domain in a list of Lennar's land banking relationships (with Millrose, Angelo Gordon, Hearthstone, Apollo and others) that he said continue to function well; Lennar said 86% of its homesites in the quarter were delivered through land bank relationships, up from 52% a year earlier, and that it controlled about 486,000 homesites versus about 11,000 owned. Domain repeats this mention on its own Press page. The Motley Fool transcript garbles 'Millrose' and 'Hearthstone'; Domain's Press page gives the clean list.
facts.source_title: Lennar Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (The Motley Fool), March 13, 2026

facts.fact: PGIM's own press release (Newark, May 26, 2026) says PGIM has surpassed $4 billion in funding for new U.S. land banking projects through its partnership with Domain, across seven completed residential land bank transactions, aimed at national homebuilders. Its 'About Domain' text says Domain has financed over 720 projects totaling about $16 billion of project costs since 2015 with more than $6 billion currently deployed; asterisked figures are footnoted as of March 31, 2026. Bob Clark is quoted as founder and CIO of Domain. The release names no builder, no deal size, no pricing and no start date.
facts.source_title: PGIM press release, 'PGIM and Domain Real Estate Partners Surpass $4 Billion in U.S. Land Banking Transactions', May 26, 2026

facts.fact: On the InsuranceAUM podcast published November 6, 2025, Bob Clark said Domain owned a little over 100,000 residential lots on behalf of builder partners, had a little over $4.7 billion invested, and had done a bit over 600 deals (the 600th closed the week before recording). He did not say whether the $4.7 billion was current or cumulative. For comparison, the April 2024 one-pager showed about 60,000 lots.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: On the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast, Bob Clark said Domain's fund was 'annualizing' at 14% to 15% and contrasted that with a dividend yield of about 9% at Millrose; he described Domain's investments as roughly four-year amortizing positions. The transcript does not say whether the 14% to 15% is gross or net.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: Insurance-capital note programme as described by Bob Clark on the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast: a first private placement to insurance investors closed at the end of 2024; a second followed in Q1 2025; in Q3 2025 Domain closed its first 'traditional' offering from its main finance company, a $200 million private placement of five-year and seven-year fixed-rate notes sold entirely to insurance capital; three transactions were done and two more were due to close in November 2025. He said the main fund entity and the private placements carry investment-grade ratings. Issuer names, coupons and buyers were not given.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: The disclaimer on the November 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast page states that Kroll assigned an investment-grade rating to Domain's operating company in May 2025, that the rating was solicited and that Domain paid for it. No rating level, rated entity name or agency release is given on the page.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 page, disclaimer

facts.fact: Credit record as stated publicly: on the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast Bob Clark said Domain had nothing on its credit watch list and no defaults in the portfolio; on the October 28, 2024 episode he said the strategy had no credit losses over its life. He also said in November 2025 that the firm had just passed 40 people.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: Structure as described by Bob Clark on the October 28, 2024 InsuranceAUM podcast: Domain closes on the land and takes title, advances funds to complete finished lots, and treats the arrangement as non-recourse project finance; the builder does the development work, guarantees timing and cost, and carries entitlement risk. Pricing was described as 'low double digits'; most deals run about four years and amortize, for an effective duration of about two to two and a half years. Deposit percentages and option-fee mechanics were not disclosed. Tagged Inferred only because the source is about 25 months old; the four-year amortizing profile was repeated in November 2025.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 251 with Bob Clark, Oct 28, 2024

facts.fact: On the October 28, 2024 InsuranceAUM podcast Bob Clark said a 2023 portfolio financing for a very large builder was done as a note rated A- (the page attributes the A- to Egan-Jones Ratings Company for a Domain subsidiary, with no compensation paid for it), and that Domain was preparing a five-year, non-call-three private placement for one builder programme. He put the land and land development financing market at roughly $150 to $160 billion. Tagged Inferred because the source is about 25 months old.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 251 with Bob Clark, Oct 28, 2024

facts.fact: FS Credit Opportunities Corp. (NYSE: FSCO) reports a first-lien senior secured loan to 'Domain Timberlake Note Issuer, LLC' (industry: Real Estate Management & Development) at Term SOFR + 6.50% with a 1.0% floor, maturing 12/20/2029: $29.0M principal at Dec 31, 2023, $20.3M at Dec 31, 2025 and $20.3M (fair value $20.1M) at June 30, 2026. The FSCO filings do not name DW Partners or Domain Real Estate Partners; the link to Domain is inferred from the entity name and from Bob Clark's statement that a Domain subsidiary issued a rated note in 2023. No document opened in this run states the affiliation, so treat the attribution as unconfirmed.
facts.source_title: FS Credit Opportunities Corp. Form N-CSRS for the period ended June 30, 2026, schedule of investments

facts.fact: What builder SEC filings reveal about Domain's terms: almost nothing. EDGAR full-text search for the exact phrase 'Domain Real Estate Partners' (2015 to Nov 19, 2026) returns a single document, Hovnanian's 10-K for fiscal 2015. A search for 'DW Partners' in 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K filings since 2019 returns no homebuilder filing (hits are FS-managed credit funds, Millrose, and unrelated energy and SPAC issuers). No public builder discloses a Domain-specific option fee, deposit or yield. (Negative finding derived from the search results.)
facts.source_title: SEC EDGAR full-text search results, queried 2026-11-19

facts.fact: Hovnanian's fiscal 2015 10-K (filed Dec 18, 2015) says it had recently announced a land banking arrangement with Domain Real Estate Partners for up to $125.0 million, under which it sells existing land parcels and holds an option to buy back finished lots subject to a cost of carry, and that such land banking transactions are accounted for as financings rather than sales because of the repurchase options. Historical (2015); tagged Inferred only for age.
facts.source_title: Hovnanian Enterprises 10-K for fiscal year ended Oct 31, 2015, Capital Resources and Liquidity

facts.fact: Millrose Properties' 10-K for fiscal 2025 does not name any competitor in its Competition section (it refers to a select number of private investment funds and asset managers), but in describing its manager it says Kennedy Lewis's in-house land banking servicer includes professionals with experience at the land banking platforms of DW Partners, LP and Blackstone Credit. 'Domain' is not mentioned.
facts.source_title: Millrose Properties, Inc. 10-K for fiscal year ended Dec 31, 2025

facts.fact: Hiring visible on Domain's own team page (21 people listed: 13 investment, 8 business and investor relations). Arrivals dated 2025-2026: Scott Shipley (May 2026; previously Co-Head of Lennar's National Land Finance Group), Bruce Rau (Nov 2025; brought on to build in-house land development capability), Tim Brown (2025; asset management), Thomas Hummel (2025; previously at Essential Housing, a TPG Angelo Gordon platform), Alok Abhilash (2025; previously Lennar), Weston Kerekes (2026; quantitative analyst), Alyssa Julian (2026; associate general counsel focused on securities and debt finance) and Krystal Lara (2025; investor relations).
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Team page

facts.fact: Two different office addresses appear in the public record: 520 Madison Avenue, 21st Floor (Domain and DW websites, 2025-2026 Form D filings) and 590 Madison Avenue, 13th Floor (Form D filings from 2022-2023 and earlier), indicating a move between 2023 and 2025.
facts.source_title: Domain website footer compared with Form D filings (Domain Real Estate Fund II 2023; Domain Solaris Fund 2026)

Florida Sunbiz returned HTTP 403; sfranalytics.com pages show no owner or address. A state entity record or deed would settle it.

The Real Deal pages returned HTTP 403 and were not opened: Keys Gate (Dec 4, 2025), a June 10, 2026 south Miami-Dade article that, per search snippet, links a DW Partners-led entity to another Homestead site, and TRD's May 27, 2026 PGIM piece. Rankings / market share: no published ranking of land bankers by size that places Domain was found. Public positioning is limited to Lennar's list of partners (March 2026) and the GSP podcast's 'one of the largest' description. The ranking search was cut short by the search budget.
Current lot count: not on Domain's website. Latest public figure is 'a little over 100,000' (Bob Clark, Nov 2025).
Investor names and insurance partners other than PGIM: not publicly disclosed. Form D filings give investor counts only.

Status of Domain Real Estate Offshore Fund I, LP (last Form D/A Dec 2022) and Domain Real Estate Fund II, LP (single Form D, May 2023): no later filings; neither appears in DW's 2026 Form ADV fund list.

Banner Ridge DSCO Private Markets Fund N-2/A filings (Feb and May 2026) hit the EDGAR full-text search for 'DW Domain' / 'Domain Servicing'; the 590,000-character document was not read through, so the context (probably a portfolio holding) is unknown.
